source_judgments: PARAMETER identifies a named constant, not a variable, coarray or procedure; a permitted pointer component does not make a structure constant a pointer entity.

C853 retains constant-expression length/bounds requirements even in a procedure. General runtime specification-expression permission does not suffice, and a variable token in a constant-property inquiry is not automatically nonconstant.
Prior value definition, including earlier definition in the same statement, is distinct from arbitrary property inquiry or name appearance; prose alone does not impose mandatory rejection.
C854 applies its four exclusions to the pointer entity, not automatically its target. Reciprocal attribute/coarray/intrinsic-role overlaps retain explicit canonical and causal gates.

C855 preserves the named-procedure-pointer subject and actual EXTERNAL attribute routes. PROCEDURE or qualifying interface declarations can already supply it; a missing keyword or link failure is not an isolated violation.
Pointer declaration, defined association, target definition, target definability, deferred parameters and procedure invocation/lifetime remain separate.
Associated deferred parameters follow the target under the exact premise; inactive-state inquiries and zero-size/zero-length definedness do not create association or available payload.
Existing CHARACTER/PDT and procedure-pointer effects are only qualified reuse candidates. No copied program, retagged role, undefined-value trap, raw address or ABI claim is introduced.
